answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock 100 tokens in a bond that remains frozen for 30 days after its last trade. Whether agents sell ocean forecasts, juniper seedlings, or jade valuations, the same rule applies. An attacker running 1,000 fake identities must immobilize 100,000 tokens and cannot reuse those bonds to replace accounts immediately. This makes a swarm costly through tied-up capital, although wealthy attackers can still afford one.
